messages:
incident-bot: P1 — inference-serving-us-east: elevated 5xx rate and request timeouts. Pager sent to @Maya. Auto-fallback to model-variant-us-east-fallback started.
Maya: saw it, joining. looking at runtime logs and routing.
Maya: symptom: spike in KV cache misses + grpc timeouts to shard-3. errors ~ 12:01 UTC.
Ryan: copying logs pls. is this a kernel/gpu OOM or network?
Maya: not OOM. network timeouts between router and shard-3 (10.4.3.12). quick log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T12:00:58Z ERROR router.go:312 rpc: context deadline exceeded -> shard-3
2026-03-15T12:01:03Z WARN cache.go:87 miss key prefix/conv/abc123
2026-03-15T12:01:05Z INFO fallback.go:44 activating model-variant-us-east-fallback
```
Sara: deployed new kernel yesterday to us-east. any relation?
Maya: unconfirmed. router telemetry shows increased latency starting ~12:00 and spikes at 12:01. I scaled router service + rebalanced 2 pods to other AZ at 12:05 as mitigation. error rate dropped but residual failures until 12:23. full recovery reported at 12:30 after a graceful rollback of one config change.
Ops Manager: need customer impact summary + suggested status page and CS copy. Also flag possible SLA credits. Maya can you summarize minutes of degraded service and list customers with >5% error rate during window?
Maya: timeline: 12:00 UTC anomaly starts; fallback triggered 12:01; scaled and rebalance 12:05; partial recovery 12:23; rollback complete 12:30; incident closed. degradation window: 12:01–12:23 (22 minutes) where error rate > threshold.
Maya: initial customer impact — most customers experienced transient errors. Two high-volume tenants (Tenant-A, Tenant-B) saw elevated 5xx for 6 and 9 minutes respectively due to pinned routing to shard-3 before routing updates applied. majority of requests were served by fallback model with slightly higher latency but no correctness regression.
CS Lead: please draft a short CS notification for impacted customers. include what happened, what we did, ETA for follow-up and whether credit is possible.
Maya: draft statuspage note (copy/paste):
"We experienced elevated errors for inference-serving in us-east between ~12:01 and 12:30 UTC. Traffic was automatically routed to a fallback model to preserve availability; some customers saw transient 5xx errors while routing updates propagated. Full service was restored by 12:30 UTC. Root cause investigation is ongoing; next update in 2 hours."
Maya: draft customer-facing note for impacted tenants:
"Hi — during today’s incident (12:01–12:23 UTC), some requests to our us-east inference endpoints returned 5xx errors before an automatic routing fallback fully engaged. We have restored full service and performed a rollback of the recent router config change to prevent recurrence. We’re assessing scope and will follow up with per-account impact and any eligible credits. If you have specific requests or see residual issues, please reply here and we’ll prioritize."
CS Lead: good. Billing — can you evaluate credit eligibility and an estimated credit amount for Tenant-A and Tenant-B?
Billing: need raw per-customer failure minutes and total monthly usage to compute. standard credit calc: eligible downtime minutes * (monthly fee) * (minutes_in_downtime / minutes_in_month) ? we typically use: credit = SLA_fraction_lapsed * monthly_commit. will confirm exact contract language per-account.
Ryan: to help billing, run this query against request-logs to get per-tenant failures during interval: 
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as failed_requests, min(ts) as first_fail, max(ts) as last_fail
FROM inference_requests
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-15T12:00:00Z' AND ts <= '2026-03-15T12:35:00Z'
AND status >= 500
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY failed_requests DESC;
```
Billing: thanks. also need per-tenant request volume to convert failures to minutes of unavailability. run: 
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, sum(request_count) as requests, avg(qps) as avg_qps
FROM tenant_usage
WHERE window_start >= '2026-03-01' AND window_end <= '2026-03-31'
AND region = 'us-east'
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```
Maya: I'll tag tenants A and B in our internal incident tracker with preliminary impact notes. ticket IDs: INC-4512 (Tenant-A impact), INC-4513 (Tenant-B impact).
Ops Manager: Billing — once you have per-tenant downtime minutes, apply contract rules: many enterprise SLAs are 99.9% availability monthly. if actual availability for the month drops below that, compute credit per contract. For smaller tenants on usage-billing we often issue one-time service rebates based on proportion of affected requests.
Billing: acknowledged. will produce a spreadsheet with columns: tenant, downtime_minutes, monthly_commit_usd, sla_threshold, eligible_credit_usd, justification. ETA 6 hours.
CS Lead: CS will send the customer-facing note tonight. for customers flagged eligible we will include: "We anticipate issuing a service credit if your contract's SLA threshold was not met. Billing will follow up with the exact credit amount and timeline."
Maya: root cause next steps: collecting router config diffs, network metrics for shard-3, and kernel change list from yesterday. assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem.
Ops Manager: internal comms template for execs (short):
"Summary: Brief us-east inference disruption on 2026-03-15 12:01–12:30 UTC. Cause: network timeouts to shard leading to routing fallback. Impact: transient 5xxs for a subset of tenants; two high-volume tenants affected longer. Mitigation: autoscaling + rebalance + rollback. Recovery: 12:30 UTC. Action: eng-runtime to root cause and follow up with timeline and mitigation plan; billing to compute credits; CS to notify customers."
Maya: assigning follow-ups: ENG-PRIORITY-1 (root cause/debug), BILL-1009 (credits calc), CS-789 (customer outbound).
oncall-bot: On-call handover reminder — @Maya please add final incident notes to runbook and assign next 24h followup.
Maya: will do. adding notes and pushing logs to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/2026-03-15/1838123456/
CS Lead: thanks everyone. keeping thread open until billing spreadsheet is posted.
Billing: uploaded preliminary spreadsheet to /shared/billing/INC-4512-4513-credits.csv. linking now.
Maya: closing incident thread for active mitigation. leaving artifacts and follow-ups for postmortem.
Ops Manager: moving to postmortems channel for RCA drafting. anyone who needs credit details or customer timelines — follow up in this thread or ping Billing/CS. :thumbsup:
